mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate resolution authorizing incorporation in Canada and appointing directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of each direct or ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) and heads of international organizations lists, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act, and, for any USD-denominated wire traffic, the OFAC SDN list. Enhanced due diligence is required for a medium-risk air cargo charter broker, including source-of-funds verification and continued transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: OnCorpus (Ontario Business Registry) for Ontario provincial corporations; for federal corporations: Corporations Canada 'Name Reservation and Search Dashboard' under Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must include a legal element in English or French: 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', 'Corporation', 'Corp.', 'Société par actions' or 's.a.' (Ontario Business Corporations Act, s. 8; Canada Business Corporations Act, s. 10). Names may be in English, French, or bilingual; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Roman letters. Distinctiveness and confusion rules apply under O. Reg. 155/06 and the CBCA Regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Ontario Companies Branch (for provincial incorporation) or with Corporations Canada's Director (for federal incorporation) within 30 days of the rejection notice, providing additional distinguishing elements or a disclaimer. If reconsideration is refused, an administrative appeal may be filed before the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (provincial) or the Federal Court (federal) within 30 days of the final refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for a statutory registered office. Ontario and federal corporate legislation require a physical street address in Ontario at which the corporation is accessible during business hours. A virtual office may be used for ancillary administrative purposes, but the registered office and the air cargo charter broker's place of business must be a substantive physical location capable of receiving service and production of corporate records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annualized unannounced physical inspection risk, based on Canada Transportation Agency audit triggers, FINTRAC AML compliance inspections, and Ontario corporate registry verification visits for regulated freight-forwarding intermediaries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16 (OBCA), ss. 4-8 (incorporation), s. 89 (share capital), s. 104 (directors), s. 115 (officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, ServiceOntario
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Articles of Incorporation under the OBCA filed through the Ontario Business Registry online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under OBCA; the Corporation may issue a single common share at nominal par value. No escrow or trust account is mandated for paid-up capital; escrow is required only where securities law exemption conditions or special subscriber arrangements so require.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. The Corporation shall adopt and file Articles of Incorporation under the Ontario Business Corporations Act and issue one hundred common shares to the subscriber under the Subscription Agreement at Canadian dollars one per share, subscription proceeds received. 2. The registered office shall be established at the address set forth in the Articles of Incorporation and recorded with the Ontario Business Registry. 3. The following persons are appointed initial directors to hold office until the first shareholders' meeting. 4. The following persons are appointed President and Secretary-Treasurer, respectively. 5. Management is authorized to complete all statutory filings, open bank accounts, and undertake regulatory licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Intellectual Property Office / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada via Ontario Business Registry name search module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online NUANS report using the Ontario Business Registry Name Search module. Select a distinct corporate name with legal element 'Inc.' or 'Corp.'; optionally submit a name reservation for 90 days before filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name rejected for identical or confusing similarity, re-file with an alternative name within the same NUANS report or proceed as a numbered Ontario corporation, e.g., 1234567 Ontario Inc.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch, ServiceOntario
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute the online Articles of Incorporation (Form 2), specifying share structure, constating provisions, registered office in Ontario, and number of directors. Pay the statutory filing fee online and submit for certification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is raised by the CIPPSB under ss. 4-5 OBCA, respond in writing within 30 days with corrected constating documents; resubmission fee applies only where the package must be reprocessed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Records Address Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the initial registered office address and records address notification. Ensure a physical, serviceable address in Ontario is maintained; notify the registry of any subsequent change by filing the prescribed change form.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Initial Notice of Registered Office Address
Lease or Occupancy Consent from Landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the address is not serviceable or landlord consent is missing, re-file with an alternative registered office address; no fee penalty applies if corrected within the statutory notice period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Finance - Corporations Information Act Central Return office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of incorporation file the Initial Return listing directors' full legal names, residential addresses, date of appointment, and officers' positions. Record board appointments in the corporate minute book under By-law No. 1.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Use the Ontario Business Registry correction/update module for any correction; a first correction within 90 days is fee-exempt. If the 60-day deadline is missed, apply to CIPPSB for an extension with extenuating circumstances evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Minute Book and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal Corporate Secretary / External Registered Law Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a minute book containing the constating documents, By-law Nos. 1 and 2, organizational resolutions, share register, transfer registers, and registered share certificates. Issue fully paid common shares and record subscription proceeds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify share allocation errors through a supplemental directors' resolution and re-issue share certificates; ensure director indemnity provisions are catalogued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online; Ontario Ministry of Finance - Employer Health Tax / Ontario Tax Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register through CRA Business Registration Online once the Certificate of Incorporation is received. Obtain a nine-digit Business Number and registrations for corporate income tax, GST/HST (if taxable supply threshold exceeds CAD 30,000), payroll source deductions, and any non-resident GST/HST. Register for Ontario Employer Health Tax and WSIB through the Ontario portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA raises a validity query or Business Number reconciliation fails, resubmit corroborating articles and corporate records via CRA My Business Account within 30 days; seek technical reconciliation through the CRA Business Window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Industry Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Toronto (or host Ontario municipality) - Municipal Licensing and Standards Division; parallel clearance from Transport Canada Civil Aviation and Canada Border Services Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence covering air freight forwarding and charter broker services. Submit zoning confirmation, office occupancy permit, proof of workplace safety program, and any CBSA sub-agent declaration. Obtain Transport Canada general operating guidance for charter broker transactions where Canadian-registered aircraft are used.
required_dossiers: List of Underlying Air Carriers or Charter Operators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If denied on zoning grounds, file a conditional use application or relocate to a permitted office use; appeal refusal through the Local Planning Appeal Tribunal within the statutory appeal period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Licensing and Standards Division (host Ontario city) with Transport Canada - Civil Aviation and Canada Border Services Agency as parallel competent authorities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for Air Cargo Charter Brokerage (Occupational Permit), combined with CBSA sub-agent registration and, where acting as a General Sales Agent for a foreign charter carrier, prior Canadian Transportation Agency clearance for sales representation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP) - Environmental Compliance Approvals Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Exempt / Class Screening: an office-based air cargo charter brokerage is excluded from the Environmental Assessment Act. Elevation to Category 2 Screening applies only if warehousing, fuel storage, or aircraft maintenance is co-located on the premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For pure office use: compliance with municipal stormwater and sewer by-laws. If warehousing is co-located: Ontario Regulation 347 for industrial and hazardous waste transfer, MECP approval for any wastewater discharge above 50 m3/day, and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions kept below the 10 megagrams per annum threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal Fire Services annual inspection and Certificate of Occupancy; structural load and life-safety engineering certification for brokerage premises and any mezzanine or warehouse deck; WSIB workplace safety insurance coverage; electrical safety certification for high-load equipment; compliance with the Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act workplace violence, emergency preparedness, and health and safety program requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and My Business Account (MyBA); Ontario corporate income tax is administered federally by the CRA under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement with the Ontario Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register online via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or electronically; a non-resident corporation must provide certified incorporation documents, foreign registration particulars, and Canadian contact/agent details. CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts: RT (GST/HST) and RC (corporate income tax). Ontario payroll source deductions and Employer Health Tax use the same BN; no separate Ontario income tax registration is required because the CRA collects Ontario corporate income tax under the collection agreement. Processing takes 2–10 business days. A non-resident may apply for optional GST/HST registration even if below the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold in order to claim input tax credits. A non-resident with no permanent establishment but carrying on business in Canada must still register for GST/HST (s.240 Excise Tax Act) and file T2 corporate returns for Canadian-source business income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an Ontario/federal Business Corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada). A resident corporation is taxed on worldwide income; a non-resident corporation is taxed on Canadian-source business income and gains from taxable Canadian property. Shareholders are not taxed on corporate income until dividends are paid, and Canada applies a partially integrated corporate-shareholder tax system. Canada does not permit check-the-box flow-through classification for corporations; the statutory definition of 'corporation' in s.248(1) ITA always yields entity-level taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (a) s.125(5.1) associated-CCPC allocation of the CAD 500,000 small business deduction (SBD) limit among associated Canadian-controlled private corporations; (b) s.256(3) designated-member election for associated corporations; (c) GST/HST s.211(1) branch/division separate supply election; (d) s.219(2) non-resident branch tax election (Part I vs. Part XIV); (e) s.216 election for rental income of non-residents; (f) hybrid mismatch disallowance rules (ss.18.2/18.4 ITA, effective 1 July 2022) — no proactive check-the-box election exists; the rules automatically deny deductions for hybrid mismatch outcomes; (g) s.150(5) short-year election and capital cost allowance elections. Canada does not offer U.S.-style check-the-box elections (Treas. Reg. 301.7701-3) for common-law corporations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (Canada); Ontario applies HST at 13% (5% federal GST component + 8% Ontario provincial component, harmonized since 1 July 2010), administered by the CRA; Ontario no longer levies a separate retail sales tax on general goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small-supplier threshold based on worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in the current calendar quarter and the immediately preceding four calendar quarters; once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration applies. Non-residents carrying on business in Canada are subject to the same threshold for supplies made in Canada (s.240 ETA); non-residents making only zero-rated exports may voluntarily register to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-clearance e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime applies to GST/HST. Canada launched a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework on the Peppol standard (from Q3 2024) through the Digital Governance Council; adoption is not a precondition for GST/HST returns. Registered corporations with annual taxable supplies over CAD 1.5M must file GST/HST returns electronically (NETFILE). Invoices and supporting records must be retained for six years (s.286 ETA). Export zero-rating does not require a government-issued tax clearance certificate, only documentary evidence of export (CBSA export declaration, air waybills, commercial invoices, and payment records).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The air-cargo charter broker may zero-rate: (1) exported goods (s.1, Part V, Sch. VI ETA) — possession and title must pass to the customer and the goods must be exported within 60 days of the supply or as soon as reasonably possible; (2) international air transportation of goods from a Canadian point to a destination outside Canada (s.20, Sch. VI), including air cargo charter fees; (3) freight-forwarding, brokerage, and customs-arrangement services supplied in respect of zero-rated international air transport (s.2, Sch. VI); and (4) services supplied to a non-resident person for use wholly outside Canada (s.7, Sch. VI). Domestic air-cargo or brokerage services that do not meet these tests are taxable at 13% HST. Zero-rating requires contemporaneous export proof: CBSA export record, master/house air waybill, commercial invoice with HS classification, charter agreement, and remittance evidence; missing or inadequate proof revives HST liability.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (CBSA G7 e-Export or CAED declaration), including AES filing for US-bound air cargo
Commercial invoice with supplier/exporter/consignee details, HS tariff classification, quantity, value, and aircraft origin-destination information
Bill of lading or master/house air waybill evidencing carriage by air from Canada to a destination outside Canada
Air cargo manifest or certificate of insurance evidencing the international carriage
Charter party agreement or broker service agreement with non-resident charterer/consignor for air cargo charter services

Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103/Fedwire record demonstrating receipt of export proceeds (documentary practice evidence; the CRA does not statutorily require a specific certificate for zero-rating)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No Canadian statute imposes a 180-day FX repatriation deadline for export proceeds; the 180-day field is a due-diligence audit benchmark — prolonged non-receipt beyond 180 days raises sham-transaction and artificial-invoice risk. The CRA may reassess GST/HST within four years (no limitation period for fraud or misrepresentation) and income tax within four years (normal), seven years (neglect), or unlimited (fraud). If zero-rating is denied on audit, the exporter is liable for uncollected HST plus interest under s.280 ETA and penalties under s.285(1) ETA of the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the understated net tax; first-time voluntary disclosure under the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program may reduce penalties if filed before audit contact. Criminal tax evasion under ss.326/327 ETA carries fines up to CAD 25,000 (summary conviction) or CAD 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years (indictment); the general anti-avoidance rule (s.274 ETA / s.245 ITA) may be invoked for artificial export arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and payment-systems authority. Canada maintains no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration: the Exchange Control Board and its statute were abolished in 1951, so there is no central-bank approval desk, FX licensing, or exchange permit regime. The Department of Finance Canada retains residual Currency Act powers; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises bank treasury and foreign-exchange risk; FINTRAC administers cross-border fund reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Ontario (Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; if no fiscal year defined, by the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 25; continuing non-compliance for 2 consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution; directors may face personal liability in respect of unpaid obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Canada Revenue Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (filing due date); balance of tax due 2 months after fiscal year-end (3 months for eligible CCPCs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax payable plus 1% per full month of delayed filing (maximum 12 months); recidivist penalty 10% plus 2% per month (max 20 months); interest charges accrued daily; directors' liability for unremitted withholdings may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ontario Corporate Tax Return (Corporations Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest and late-filing penalties per the Ontario Corporations Tax Act; failure to file may result in a default assessment and loss of loss carry-forward benefits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Ontario Business Corporations Act, all corporations must appoint an auditor at each annual general meeting unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, waive the appointment by unanimous resolution in respect of that financial year; where no waiver exists, a mandatory independent audit is required. CRA may also require an audit where gross revenue exceeds CAD 100,000 and seeks additional assurance; lenders or air freight counterparties typically impose audit clauses for finance facility or charter contract limits.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises or as required by regulators; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) permitted for non-publicly accountable corporations; consistent application with CRA's GAAP requirement for computing taxable income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing for OBCA corporations as of the effective date; however, Canada's Bill C-42 introduced a federal beneficial ownership registry under the Canada Business Corporations Act, requiring annual confirmation of individuals with significant control (vote rights, board influence, ownership >25%) as part of the CBCA annual return. Ontario-based federally incorporated corporations must file such confirmation annually with Corporations Canada; extra-provincially registered Ontario corporations are subject to federal UBO disclosure only where CBCA applies. Transfer of shares must be recorded in the Register of Members and any deemed significant control changes updated within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (inclusive of share transfer history)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (where CBCA applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150 - CAD 400 per year (approx. USD 112 - USD 300)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 3,500 - CAD 12,000 per year (approx. USD 2,600 - USD 9,000) for a mid-cap air cargo charter broker with a single operating entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC) on first CAD 500,000 of active business income (reduced federal rate to 9% and Ontario rate to 3.2%); investment tax credits for scientific research and experimental development; no general tax holidays.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via CRA's e-file (approved software) or NETFILE
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross receipts from all business activities)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income; for non-resident corporations, only Canadian-source income is taxable unless treaty applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses (deductible business expenses, including charter costs, fuel, insurance, and administrative overhead)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses reasonably incurred to earn Canadian-source income; allocate expenses per treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (revenue minus expenses and adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Canadian tax rules; non-residents may be subject to Part I tax on Canadian business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and provincial tax payable (before credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate federal and Ontario tax; non-residents may be subject to branch tax under Part XIV.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, investment tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance due plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeated failure penalty of 10% plus 2% per month; interest on unpaid amounts at prescribed rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII tax on dividends paid to non-residents)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident shareholder must provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority; submit Form NR301 (for US) or NR302 (for other countries) to the CRA; the payer must withhold at the reduced treaty rate if the recipient is eligible and the forms are completed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, reduced to 10% under Canada-US treaty (for certain IP); interest: statutory 25%, reduced to 15% under Canada-US treaty (arm's length interest may be exempt).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for goods transactions and CAD 500,000 for services transactions with non-residents (aggregate per year) trigger mandatory Local File / Master File preparation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) like OECD jurisdictions, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) applies; transactions must have genuine economic substance to avoid reassessment and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false statements, or fraudulent claims in tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under the Income Tax Act: fines up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No real economic substance, used for tax avoidance, money laundering, or treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess and apply GAAR; penalties up to 50% of tax avoided; criminal charges for fraud; corporate veil may be pierced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for corporate debts if they allowed the company to operate without substance; potential imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to report large cash transactions (over CAD 10,000) or suspicious transactions to FINTRAC; inadequate compliance program
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for individuals and CAD 2,000,000 for corporations; criminal penalties for willful non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for penalties if they failed to ensure compliance; may face criminal charges and imprisonment.
